headline: LME Copper Prices Rebound 0.7% from Seven-Month Low on Low Chinese Inventories
summary: Benchmark copper on the London Metal Exchange rose 0.7% to $12,558 per ton, recovering from seven-month lows as Chinese warehouse inventories fell to three-year lows.
why: Copper is an industrial metal used heavily in electrical grid infrastructure, electronics, and construction.

impacts.name: Copper
impacts.why: LME benchmark copper contracts rebounded 0.7% following buying after prices hit seven-month lows.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Depressed inventory levels in China attracted buyers, prompting a price rebound off recent multi-month lows.
